text:
Buffalo is the most average team in the league right now, and that is the problem. The Sabres are 11-10-4 with 26 points, and our expected points say exactly 26: no luck either way. They get 50% of the expected goals at 5v5 and score almost precisely what their chances deserve. Nothing here is a mirage, which also means nothing is about to bounce back on its own.

The good news lives up front. Tage Thompson has been scoring in bunches, extending a goal streak with two in one night, and Jack Quinn keeps adding to his totals. The line that has driven play best is Quinn with Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson, which gets 59% of the expected goals and has outscored teams 9-4. Jiri Kulich, after a slow start, has become a real center between Benson and Thompson; he had a goal and an assist in Wednesday's 5-1 win over the Rangers, with Rasmus Dahlin scoring 17 seconds in.

The worry is the net and the penalty kill. Alex Lyon lost three straight before that win, and the Sabres allow 0.81 expected goals a game shorthanded, one of the weaker kills in our numbers.

Lindy Ruff's team is 4-5-1 in its last 10, and our simulations give it a 32% chance at the playoffs. What to watch: whether the Kulich line keeps producing, because a second scoring line is the only way out of the middle.
headline: Sabres stuck in the middle, again
